clue.text: Short outburst by posh type in Countdown finale

indicators.note: short means cut off before the end, so the word for outburst loses its last letter

parts.note: a blast is a sudden outburst
a toff is British slang for an upper-class person

explanation.surface: A snooty contestant has a brief tantrum at the end of the TV quiz Countdown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Countdown' looks like the British TV quiz, but here it is a launch countdown, whose last moment is the lift-off.
explanation.definitionFit: A rocket launch follows a countdown, so the launch itself is the countdown's climax.

clue.text: Available men work on crash below without women

indicators.note: to work on something is to reshape it, so these letters are rearranged
without means the letter for women is left out of the pool

explanation.surface: Single men toil after a crash, with no women around.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the letters of CRASH BELOW, remove the W (women), and rearrange the remaining nine.
explanation.definitionFit: Unmarried men are available as partners, the sense in which single men are eligible.

clue.text: Remove sections of a craft's control room

parts.note: the bridge is where a ship is steered from

explanation.surface: An instruction to strip out parts of a ship's command centre.
explanation.definitionFit: To shorten a text by cutting passages out of it is the editing sense of the verb.

clue.text: Irritated at dire RAF sales show

indicators.note: irritated letters are stirred up and disturbed, so these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone annoyed at a dreadful Royal Air Force sales event.
explanation.definitionFit: An exhibition where firms show and sell goods to other businesses is a trade event of this kind.

clue.text: Tact shown when penalties put on abandoned storehouse

indicators.note: in a down answer one piece is put on top of the next, so the penalties come first

parts.note: fines are monetary penalties

indicators.note: an abandoned storehouse is emptied, leaving only its outer letters

explanation.surface: Tactfulness is needed when charges are levied on a derelict warehouse.
explanation.definitionFit: Delicate skill in handling people is both tact and finesse; they are synonyms.

clue.text: Leaves jewellery which has changed hands

indicators.note: changing hands swaps left for right, so the L in the jewellery word becomes R

parts.note: a locket is a pendant worn as jewellery

explanation.surface: Someone abandons a piece of jewellery that has been sold on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' reads as a verb; it is salad leaves. L and R are the usual abbreviations for left and right.
explanation.definitionFit: Rocket, also called arugula, is a peppery salad green sold as a bag of leaves.

clue.text: Animal moved quickly in zero gravity at first

parts.note: O looks like the figure zero
ran means moved quickly

indicators.note: at first takes only the opening letter of gravity

explanation.surface: A creature dashed about in weightlessness at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: An orang is a short form of orangutan, a great ape and so an animal.

clue.text: Distance not a barrier for clever clogs

parts.note: K stands for a kilometre, as in a 10K run
no means not a, as in 'he's no expert'
a wall is a barrier

explanation.surface: Distance is no obstacle for a smart person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clever clogs' is British slang for a smug person who thinks they know everything.
explanation.definitionFit: A clever clogs is a smart alec, someone who claims to have every fact; the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Flyer needs a bearing to find the distant moon

parts.note: a tit is a small bird, which flies
N, north, is a compass bearing

explanation.surface: A pilot needs a compass heading to reach a faraway moon.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturn's largest satellite carries this name, and it lies far from Earth.

clue.text: The Swan seen at night craftily evacuating onto cattle

indicators.note: evacuating empties the word craftily, leaving its first and last letters

parts.note: gnus, or wildebeest, are a kind of wild cattle

explanation.surface: A swan spotted after dark sneakily settling on some cows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'onto' puts the first piece on top of the second in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The constellation of the Swan, visible in the night sky, has the Latin name for swan.

clue.text: Without doubt involved in chance RTA in Lyons

indicators.note: involved in says the letters sit inside the phrase chance RTA in Lyons

explanation.surface: There was surely a chance of a road accident in the French city of Lyons.
explanation.walkthrough: RTA is British shorthand for a road traffic accident.
explanation.definitionFit: Surely and definitely both mean without doubt, synonyms of the adverb.

clue.text: Metal frequently used in the past at high altitude

parts.note: Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium
oft is an old word for often, now archaic

explanation.surface: A metal that was once commonly used at great heights.
explanation.definitionFit: Up in the air, high overhead, is the meaning of this adverb.

clue.text: The Eagle perhaps finally landed in eastern pass

indicators.note: in places that letter within the other pieces

parts.note: to pass away is to die

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of landed

explanation.surface: The Eagle lunar module has at last landed in an eastern mountain pass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Eagle' suggests Apollo 11's lander, but it is the nickname of Eddie Edwards, the British ski jumper famous at the 1988 Winter Olympics.
explanation.definitionFit: Eddie Edwards was dubbed the Eagle; 'perhaps' signals that he is one example of someone so nicknamed.

clue.text: Tiny bit of beach is place to have time out with good weather

indicators.note: out removes a letter, so the time letter leaves the word for place

parts.note: a stand is a place or position
rain is a kind of weather

explanation.surface: The beach is a spot for a break, in good weather.
explanation.definitionFit: A single granule from the shore is the smallest unit of a sandy beach.

clue.text: Work with old and extremely polite judge

indicators.note: extremely takes the extreme letters, first and last, of polite

parts.note: to rate is to judge or assess

explanation.surface: Work alongside an elderly, very courteous judge.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that works is said to function, the same sense as run or work.

clue.text: Unhealthy peeling flesh. Get cutting implements!

parts.note: sick means unhealthy

indicators.note: peeling strips off the skin, so flesh loses its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A grisly cry: sickly skin is coming off, so fetch the knives!
explanation.definitionFit: Curved blades for cutting grass or crops are reaping tools, a kind of cutting implement.

clue.text: Space Traveller magazine article kept by fan

parts.note: Cosmo is the short name of Cosmopolitan magazine

indicators.note: kept by means the article is held inside the word for fan

parts.note: a nut is an enthusiast, as in a fitness nut
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A sci-fi magazine piece held by an admirer.
explanation.definitionFit: A Soviet or Russian astronaut is a traveller in space.

clue.text: Unregulated Net is said to be thoroughly cleansed

indicators.note: unregulated letters are out of order, so these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: The wild internet is claimed to have been scrubbed clean.
explanation.definitionFit: Disinfected and scrubbed clean, made hygienic, is the meaning of this past participle.

clue.text: Arctic region's small peninsula

parts.note: Iberia is the peninsula holding Spain and Portugal

explanation.surface: A cold northern area is a modest peninsula.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after region stands for 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The vast Russian territory east of the Urals stretches to the Arctic Ocean.

clue.text: Sponge served on seaside structure is less smooth

parts.note: to bum is to cadge or sponge off others
a pier is a walkway jutting into the sea at a resort

explanation.surface: A sponge cake eaten on the pier is lumpier than expected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sponge' looks like cake or a bath sponge; it is the verb to cadge.
explanation.definitionFit: A rougher road or ride, more jolting, is the comparative of an adjective for uneven.

clue.text: Voyage with a part of survey absent?

definitions.meaning: a journey into space, like the moon landings
a cryptic reading: ..., a piece of the polling that is missing, run together

explanation.surface: A trip on which some of the questionnaire went missing.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer as A POLL OMISSION, sharing the O; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apollo programme's flights to the moon were each a journey through space.

clue.text: See 20
Ms Markle about to get rid of husband gaining weight

indicators.note: about means the name goes round the word to
get rid of removes the husband letter from the name

parts.note: Meghan Markle, the Duchess of Sussex

explanation.surface: The Duchess of Sussex is about to lose her husband and put on pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit equal to a million tons, used for the explosive force of bombs, is a measure of weight.

clue.text: Motivate one attending NASA (paid regularly by engineers)

indicators.note: by places the engineers beside the rest, at the end

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter, starting from the first

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: Encourage a worker at NASA, whose salary comes regularly from engineers.
explanation.definitionFit: To fill someone with the urge to act is to stir or encourage them.

clue.text: Pioneer in storm rang off

indicators.note: off means gone wrong or awry, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pioneer caught in a storm hung up the phone.
explanation.walkthrough: Neil Armstrong was the first person to walk on the moon, a pioneer of space travel.
explanation.definitionFit: The first man on the moon was a trailblazer, a pioneer in exploration.

clue.text: Adjust coverage of radar missing outer reaches of planet

indicators.note: missing outer drops the first and last letters of radar
the outer reaches of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Change the radar's range so it no longer covers the edges of the planet.
explanation.definitionFit: To modify something to suit new conditions is to adjust it.

clue.text: Can bring up example to demonstrate colour

parts.note: a tin is a can

indicators.note: in a down answer, bringing up reads the letters from the bottom upwards

parts.note: eg is the abbreviation for 'for example'

explanation.surface: A tin can raise an instance that shows a hue.
explanation.definitionFit: A slight shade or trace of a colour is a tint.

clue.text: Appearance possibly in part of the film studio

parts.note: on can mean in, as in on stage
a set is the built scene in a film studio

explanation.surface: Perhaps an actor's appearance on the studio set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appearance' suggests an actor's cameo; it means a beginning, as in the appearance of symptoms.
explanation.definitionFit: The first appearance of something, especially an illness, marks its start.

clue.text: 23 Across returned to track a Clanger?

indicators.note: to track is to follow behind, so the reversed name comes after a
returned means the name is read backwards

parts.note: the answer at 23 Across is the astronaut whose first name is Neil

explanation.surface: An astronaut comes back to follow a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: The Clangers were knitted creatures from a moon in a British children's TV show, so one is an extraterrestrial; 'clanger' also means a blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: A creature from another world is extraterrestrial, as the Clangers of the TV show were.

clue.text: Smooth talkers in considerable number with hair so made-up

parts.note: a lot is a considerable number

indicators.note: made-up letters are invented anew, so hair so is rearranged

explanation.surface: Many charmers with hair so styled and dressed up.
explanation.definitionFit: Womanising seducers are named after the rake Lothario in an 18th-century play, smooth-tongued men.

clue.text: The Right Stuff that is within half of aviators

indicators.note: stuff means pack something inside another piece
within says the stuffing sits inside the other letters
half of takes the back half of the word aviators

parts.note: ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A nod to the astronaut film The Right Stuff, about pilots.
explanation.walkthrough: The Right Stuff is a film about test pilots and astronauts; here 'The Right' is the definition and 'Stuff' the insertion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the British Conservative Party are on the right of politics.

clue.text: Don't need to re-enter in a continuous sequence

indicators.note: re-entering the letters puts them back in a new order

explanation.surface: A capsule need not re-enter the atmosphere again and again.
explanation.definitionFit: Lined up with each end touching the next, one after another, describes an unbroken run.
